correctness.rationale: All-parameter gap lemma: cyclic gaps q+s_i with sum s_i=2 exhaust the states; legal slides transfer 1 or 2 gap units, giving four distinct neighbors. A complete local two-hole transfer case table specifies the links of all graph triangles and quadrilaterals and isolates double-transfer A-A boundary edges. This proves a compact connected surface. Double-counting gives V=n(m+1)/2, E=n(m+1), F3=n, F4=n(m-1)/2, chi=0; boundary A_x adjacent A_{x±q}, giving gcd(n,q)=gcd(2,q) components; surface classification finishes. Distinct independent state enumeration and gap-transfer implementations check the critical local lemma and full graph for multiple k,m. Finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new content is the explicit square-triangle polygonal completion of maximum-independent-set token-sliding for the two-excess-position family of power cycles and the topological Mobius/annulus parity dichotomy, including exact counts and boundary monodromy. Bonsma et al. provide reachability methods for claw-free graphs, not this surface classification. Avis--Hoang address structural TS_k problems including *ordinary* cycles C_n rather than the higher graph powers C_n^k and do not give a square-triangle compact surface for this two-defect family. Search result identifiers document likely analogues but imply no direct coverage. The residual risk is an equivalent formulation in unindexed exclusion-process or configuration-space literature.

value.rationale: The close-packed exclusion process on a ring has its first interacting two-vacancy state space at n=(k+1)m+2. The result determines the entire two-dimensional cell structure formed by its shortest reconfiguration loops and exhibits a topological orientation transition (Möbius versus annulus) driven by parity of the exclusion distance. Exact face counts and boundary monodromy give a transferable description, not a narrow isolated numerical example or textbook substitution.
